subject: general
question: Which is the sixth of the eighteen books of the Indian epic Mahabharata (written by Vyasa) that contains the widely studied Bhagavad Gita?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Bhishma Parva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhishma Parva**

 
 
• India's ancient holy epic,** The Mahabharata**, is undoubtedly the most well-known work of Indian literature.
 
• The epic, attributed to the poet **Vyasa**, has **18 sections and more than 220,000 lines**.
 
• The **sixth of the Mahabharata's eighteen books** is the **Bhishma Parva**, often known as the Book of Bhishma.
 
• It is the only Parva in the Mahabharata where **Bhishma and Krishna**, rather than Karna, serve as the main heroes.
 
• Traditionally, this epic includes **122 chapters and 4 parts.**
 
• The **Bhagavad Gita**, also known as Gita, The Song of the Lord, or The Celestial Song, is a well-known chapter of the Mahabharata.
 
• The **Mahabharata's battles **are the background for the religious literature known as the Bhagavad Gita. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• The Bhagavad Gita, also known as the **"Song of God,"** is a long poem composed of **701 Sanskrit couplets**.
 
• It has chapters that detail **Arjuna's reflections** on the meaning of life, the purpose of war, and the ultimate effects of warfare.
 
• Other treatises in the Bhishma Parva discuss **tactics and strategy as well as the just war theory of ancient India**.
